name: ANLI
desc: Three rounds of human-written NLI examples that fooled the strongest model of the previous round; still unsaturated.

name: CommitmentBank (CB)
desc: Tiny 3-way entailment set about embedded clauses — how committed is the speaker to the clause being true?

name: MultiNLI
desc: 433k NLI pairs across ten genres (fiction, government, telephone speech, …) with matched and mismatched test sets.

name: QNLI
desc: SQuAD recast as a binary task: does this Wikipedia sentence contain the answer to this question?

name: RTE
desc: The small, hard, classic entailment set from the PASCAL/TAC challenges; in both GLUE and SuperGLUE.

name: SciTail
desc: 27k entailment pairs built from science-exam questions and web sentences; no neutral class.

name: SNLI
desc: 570k human-written sentence pairs labelled entailment, contradiction or neutral; the first large-scale NLI corpus.

name: BoolQ
desc: 16k naturally occurring yes/no questions from Google search, each paired with a Wikipedia passage.

name: CoQA
sota_model: RoBERTa + AT + KD ensemble (Zhuiyi) / TR-MT (WeChat AI)
desc: 127k questions in 8k multi-turn conversations about a passage; each question depends on the ones before it.

name: DROP
desc: 96k questions that need counting, sorting, dates or arithmetic over a Wikipedia paragraph; answers are numbers, dates or spans.

name: MultiRC
desc: Questions with several candidate answers, any number of which can be correct; answering needs more than one sentence.

name: QuAC
desc: Teacher–student dialogues about a hidden Wikipedia section; 100k questions, many unanswerable, still below human level.

name: RACE
desc: 100k multiple-choice questions from Chinese middle- and high-school English exams; answers often need reasoning over the whole passage.

name: ReCoRD
desc: 120k cloze-style queries over CNN/Daily Mail articles; fill the masked entity in a sentence that needs commonsense.

name: SQuAD 2.0
desc: SQuAD plus 50k unanswerable questions written to look answerable; the model must extract a span or abstain.

name: Natural Questions
desc: 300k real Google queries with Wikipedia answers; the closed-book 'NQ-Open' variant asks the model to answer from memory.

name: TriviaQA
desc: 95k trivia questions written by enthusiasts, with Wikipedia and web evidence; the standard closed-book knowledge probe.

name: WebQuestions
desc: 6k questions from the Google Suggest API answered against Freebase; the oldest open-domain QA set still in use.

name: ARC
desc: 7.8k grade-school science questions; the Challenge split holds the ones retrieval and co-occurrence methods got wrong.

name: COPA
desc: 1,000 tiny causal puzzles: given a premise, which of two alternatives is the more plausible cause or effect?

name: HellaSwag
desc: Pick the most plausible continuation of a scene from four options; wrong options were machine-generated to fool BERT.

name: OpenBookQA
desc: 6k science questions that need one 'open book' fact plus commonsense the book does not contain.

name: PIQA
desc: Choose the sensible way to accomplish an everyday physical goal — 'to separate egg whites…' — from two solutions.

name: Story Cloze
sota_model: Li et al. 2019 (as cited in GPT-3)
desc: Given four sentences of a five-sentence story, choose the right fifth sentence from two candidates.

name: Winograd Schema Challenge
desc: 273 hand-crafted pronoun-resolution puzzles where one word flips the answer; the classic test of commonsense.

name: WinoGrande
desc: 44k Winograd-style fill-in-the-blank items, crowd-sourced then adversarially filtered; still a standard LLM metric.

name: Children's Book Test
desc: Twenty sentences of a children's book, then a 21st with a word missing; choose it from ten candidates. Scored on common nouns and named entities.

name: enwik8
desc: The first 100 MB of a raw Wikipedia XML dump, scored in bits per byte; the character-level compression benchmark.

name: LAMBADA
desc: Predict the last word of a passage that humans can guess only with the full context, never from the last sentence alone.

name: One Billion Word
desc: 800M words of shuffled news sentences with an 800k vocabulary; the big sentence-level LM benchmark of 2014–2019.

name: Penn Treebank
desc: 1M words of Wall Street Journal text with a 10k vocabulary and no punctuation; the oldest LM benchmark still reported.

name: text8
desc: enwik8 stripped to lower-case letters and spaces only — 27 symbols, 100M characters.

name: WikiText-103
desc: 103M words of Wikipedia articles with a 267k vocabulary; the standard large word-level perplexity benchmark of the Transformer-XL era.

name: WikiText-2
desc: 2M words of Good/Featured Wikipedia articles with punctuation, case and numbers preserved; the small word-level LM benchmark.

name: CoLA
desc: 10k sentences from linguistics textbooks marked grammatical or not; scored by Matthews correlation.

name: MRPC
desc: 5.8k news sentence pairs labelled as paraphrases or not; small, imbalanced, part of GLUE.

name: QQP
desc: 400k pairs of Quora questions labelled duplicate or not; the big paraphrase task in GLUE.

name: SST-2
desc: 67k movie-review phrases labelled positive or negative; the standard sentiment benchmark.

name: STS-B
desc: 8.6k sentence pairs rated 0–5 for similarity; the one regression task in GLUE.

name: WiC
desc: Does the same word mean the same thing in these two sentences? 7.5k pairs; still below human level.

name: GLUE
sota_model: Vega v1 (JD Explore) · Turing ULR v6 (Microsoft)
desc: Nine sentence-level tasks and one leaderboard score; the benchmark GPT-1 and BERT were measured on.

name: SuperGLUE
desc: GLUE's harder successor: eight tasks (BoolQ, CB, COPA, MultiRC, ReCoRD, RTE, WiC, WSC) chosen because BERT still failed them.

name: CNN / Daily Mail
desc: 300k news articles paired with their bullet-point highlights; the default abstractive summarisation benchmark.

name: WMT Translation
sota: Fr→En 39.2 (GPT-3) · En→Fr 45.6 (Edunov 2018) · De→En 40.6 (GPT-3) · En→De 41.2 (Wang 2018) · Ro→En 39.9 (mBART) · En→Ro 38.5 (mBART)
desc: Shared-task test sets for French, German and Romanian ↔ English; scored in BLEU. GPT-2 tried Fr–En, GPT-3 all three pairs.

name: GPT-3 synthetic tasks
desc: Tasks the GPT-3 authors invented to probe in-context learning: 2–5 digit arithmetic, unscrambling words, SAT analogies, and human detection of generated news.
